assessment: The response demonstrates strong quantitative fundamentals: correct wholesale pricing ($33/unit), contribution math ($28,000 or $14/unit vs. $33/unit direct), and a feasible eight-week cash and inventory plan that preserves the $16,000 reserve and correctly identifies that the retailer deposit covers the supplier deposit plus freight. Its main weakness is risk analysis: replenishment slippage and defect returns go unaddressed, the default-loss framing is materially wrong (defaulting produces a ~$5,000 net loss, not merely lost profit), and credit protections (trade references, MAP) are relatively weak given the unsecured $33,000 exposure and thin 200-unit stock buffer. A smaller first order or stronger deposit terms would materially improve the risk profile.
judge_agreement: All five judges agreed the core arithmetic and cash/stock mapping were correct, with broad consensus around unit economics (median 8) and cash planning (median 8); most noted the missing aggregate direct-retail comparison and minor timeline imprecision as secondary. On risk, four of five judges converged on 4–6, consistently citing the absent replenishment-slippage and defect risks; Gemini was the clear outlier, scoring 8–10 across all criteria and treating omissions other judges saw as material. No rule errors were flagged by any judge.
